---
title: "Services"
description: "Independent review, methods and assessments, and research partnerships for environmental questions, from research groups to homeowners."
---

The tools on this site are free. What we charge for is the thinking behind them: working out what a question really needs, building methods where none exist, and checking that conclusions hold up.

Every engagement starts with a short written scope that sets out the question, deliverables, timeline and price before any work begins.

## Review: independent second opinions

A fixed-scope, fixed-price check by someone with no stake in the outcome. It's the simplest way to work with us.

- **Grant proposals.** Pre-submission review of aims, methods, feasibility and whether the budget matches the work.
- **Research and sampling design.** Sample size, spatial layout, statistical power, and whether the design can answer the question being asked.
- **Models.** Statistical, geostatistical and process models: assumptions, validation, overfitting and data leakage, and how uncertainty is handled.
- **Data.** Quality, gaps, harmonisation problems, and whether the data supports the claims made from it.
- **Reports and manuscripts.** Pre-submission review of the analysis and the inference drawn from it.
- **Consultant deliverables.** A check of a study you have paid for, such as a flood, soil or site assessment, before you act on it. Short second opinions are available for homeowners as well.

We only review work for the people who own it: applicants, authors or clients. We don't take paid reviews of proposals or manuscripts we are assessing for a funder or journal, and everything you share stays confidential.

## Build: methods and assessments

For questions that off-the-shelf methods don't answer, or places where the usual data doesn't exist.

- **Method development.** Designing, validating and documenting a method for a problem without an established solution.
- **Assessments in data-scarce settings.** Soil and landscape maps, hydrologic soil groups, curve number and retention surfaces for hydrological models, soil-water flux, and carbon stocks, all delivered with uncertainty.
- **Updating and harmonising existing data.** Bringing legacy surveys, mixed depths and mixed methods into one consistent dataset. Maps are updated, not started again.
- **Geostatistics and analysis.** Kriging, mixed models, model validation, and fixing problem datasets.
- **Decision support.** Combining sources of uncertainty into decision maps, prioritising areas, and plain-language summaries for the people who have to act.
- **Advanced versions of our tools.** Continuous rather than discrete calculations, uncertainty propagation, and custom builds of the free tools.

Methods are interpretable "glass-box" functions benchmarked against machine-learning alternatives, so every result can be traced and checked. Clients receive a licence to use the methods and results built for them. RafikiArdhi keeps the methods themselves and may later release an open version.

Engineering work that requires a licensed professional engineer is carried out alongside that engineer.

## Partner: research collaboration

- **Analytical partnerships.** Ongoing methods, analysis and modelling support for research groups and projects, with co-authorship where the contribution warrants it.
- **Methods lead on proposals.** Writing the methods and analysis sections of a proposal, with RafikiArdhi named in the team and budget as the analytical partner.

## Learn: training

- **Workshops** in soil classification, digital soil mapping, data harmonisation, uncertainty and R, tailored to the group and available in several languages.
